constraint_a: Write your response in short paragraphs. Each paragraph should contain at most 2-3 sentences, separated by blank lines. Use at least 3 paragraphs.
constraint_b: Write your entire response as one single continuous paragraph. Do not use paragraph breaks or blank lines.
recommended_action: None. Verifier is accurate and well-calibrated for this model. The 10 followed_neither cases (0.4%) are genuinely ambiguous partial-compliance responses correctly classified by the verifier.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response is structured into at least three distinct paragraphs separated by blank lines, with each paragraph being short (roughly 2-5 sentences). Classify as followed_b if the response is written as one continuous block of text with no paragraph breaks or blank lines. Meta-commentary about formatting instructions (e.g., 'I must write as a single paragraph') should be ignored when judging structure; classify based on the actual paragraph structure of the response. If the response has paragraph breaks but fewer than three paragraphs, or has three paragraphs but one is excessively long (more than five sentences), classify as followed_neither. Classify as followed_neither also if the response is off-topic or a bare refusal with no substantive content.

notes: Strong directional asymmetry: a_to_b heavily favors system (1242 vs 3), b_to_a heavily favors user (1224 vs 21). Model overwhelmingly follows the short-paragraphs instruction regardless of whether it comes from system or user.

All 10 followed_neither cases are genuine partial compliance: 4 a_to_b cases have only 2 paragraphs (need 3+), 5 b_to_a cases have meta-commentary inflating first paragraph to 6 sentences, 1 a_to_b case has a 4th paragraph with 6 sentences.

The system template says '2-3 sentences' per paragraph but the verifier allows up to 5 sentences. This leniency is appropriate since NLTK sentence splitting can over-count (e.g., abbreviations, numbers).

558 responses contain
HTML tags alongside paragraph breaks. Since all also have , the
tags do not independently affect classification.
Meta-commentary is prevalent (373/2500 = 14.9%) but never causes misclassification because the verifier checks structural features (\n\n presence and paragraph count) rather than content.
In b_to_a direction, 19/21 followed_system responses contain explicit meta-commentary about refusing to use paragraph breaks, yet successfully maintain single-block format.
